newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts hit by European weakness, await GDP data.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts hit by European weakness, await GDP data.

text.p: UK government bond (gilt) futures eased back with other European bonds in early trade as the markets worried about the chances of European monetary union.

Overnight comments from Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer that the U.S. economy was growing too fast and that the Japanese Ministry of Finance had order Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co to halt its operations, also hurt sentiment.
"You'd have to be pretty brave to buy bonds today," one gilt trader said. By 0738 GMT, LIFFE June gilts were down 2/32 at 108-31/32.

But gilts were slightly outperforming Bunds, after the gilt/Bund spread move out to 191 basis points on Thursday. Gilts had recouped some ground in relative terms and the spread was at 190 basis points this morning.
"I think we're going to do a bit better than yesterday and that the future is likely to be busy. It's looking pretty quiet on the cash though," one gilt salesman at a UK brokerage said.
The gilt market has solid support at aru=ound 108-14/32.
At the short end of the yield curve, LIFFE June short sterling was down one basis point at 93.35 as the market pretty much discounts a 50 basis point rise in interest rates.
First quarter UK GDP data are due at 0830 GMT will provide something for the market to focus on but are not expected to be a major factor.
The Reuters consensus forecast is for GDP growth of 0.9 percent, giving a year-on-year rise of 2.9 percent.
A lively services sector is expected to lead the way while industrial production is likely to be constrained by lower energy output due to unusually mild weather.
